twins.note: Snowboarder — rents at Valle Nevado this trip.

twins.name: Henri
twins.note: rents skis at Valle Nevado — no ski bag on the plane

twins.name: Renée
twins.note: 15 — intermediate: comfortable blues/reds, not powder. Rents skis.

twins.title: BRU → SCL
twins.description: No direct flight. Overnight/evening arrival.

twins.title: Fly BRU → Santiago
twins.notes: ~17h with 1–2 stops (Iberia via Madrid, Air France via Paris, KLM via Amsterdam, Delta, Turkish). July = peak — book by Jan 2027, expect ~$1,400–1,800 pp RT.

twins.title: Stay: Las Condes / Providencia
twins.description: Closer to the G-21 mountain road for Day 4. Light stroll, early night — jetlag + start of acclimatisation at ~500 m.

twins.title: Cerro San Cristóbal
twins.description: The city from above: teleférico up to the 880 m summit, the Andes on one side and Gran Torre on the other. Morning light is best — the cordillera glows.

twins.title: Mercado Central
twins.description: Lunch at the iron-built 1872 market — congrio frito or a big bowl of chupe de mariscos, standing at the counter like the locals. Fish market chaos, zero tourist markup if you pick the busy stalls.

twins.title: Sky Costanera at sunset
twins.description: Top of Latin America's tallest tower at golden hour — the whole 6,000 m Andes wall turns pink behind the city. Go 45 min before sunset, it gets busy.

twins.title: Shuttle Santiago → Valle Nevado
twins.description: 90 min. Leave before 13:00 — the G-21 access road only allows uphill traffic in the morning window.

twins.title: Stay: self-catered studio, ski-in/out
twins.description: ~$330–420/nt (or Farellones for budget). 4-day ski pass: weekday ~$33/day, weekend ~$55.

twins.title: Transfer to Valle Nevado + warm-up
twins.notes: **G-21 road: up-window 08:00–13:00.** Shared shuttle SCL→VN (~$35–40 pp, 90 min). Afternoon: rental fitting + one gentle warm-up run — first exposure at 3,000 m, take it easy.

twins.title: Valle Nevado full day
twins.description: Renée: groomed blues/reds front side (25% intermediate terrain). Henri: advanced bowls. Niko: wide groomers. Hydrate, layers, sunscreen — altitude sun is brutal.

twins.title: Valle Nevado + La Parva
twins.description: One pass covers the interconnected terrain — La Parva adds intermediate cruising + big views. Weather-chase: pick the side with best visibility.

twins.title: Ski day 3 (morning) → Santiago
twins.notes: **G-21 down-window 15:00–20:00.** Morning ski, lunch at the resort, transfer down ~15:00. Night near SCL airport for the morning flight.

twins.title: LATAM SCL → CUZ (direct)
twins.description: ~2h30–3h30. The stitch that makes this trip work.

twins.title: Stay: Urubamba / Ollantaytambo — 3 nights
twins.description: Sacred Valley at 2,800 m — the gentle altitude ramp.

twins.title: SCL → CUZ → Sacred Valley
twins.notes: The linchpin flight: LATAM direct, daily in season, ~2h30–3h30 — book a morning departure. Then the **critical acclimatisation move**: transfer straight to the Sacred Valley (~1.5h, 2,800 m) instead of sleeping in Cusco (3,400 m).

twins.title: Pisac ruins + artisan market
twins.description: The hillside citadel above the town — terraces, temples and the famous Sunday artisan market at the foot. The ruins are the morning's altitude-friendly warm-up (2,900 m).

twins.title: Maras salt mines + Moray terraces
twins.description: Thousands of salt ponds terraced into the canyon, worked by hand since pre-Inca times. One of the most photogenic half-hours in Peru.

twins.title: Vistadome train (PeruRail) — 1h45
twins.description: Ollantaytambo → Aguas Calientes.

twins.title: Stay: Aguas Calientes
twins.description: Inkaterra / Casa del Sol / El Mapi.

twins.title: Stay: Cusco — 4 nights
twins.description: 3,400 m — the family is pre-acclimatised from Valle Nevado + Sacred Valley.

twins.title: Machu Picchu
twins.notes: Sunrise bus (first 5:30 am), guided tour, optional Huayna Picchu hike (permit — book Jan–Feb 2027!). Mid-afternoon train back + transfer to Cusco.

twins.title: Cusco walking tour
twins.description: Plaza de Armas → the 12-angled stone of Hatun Rumiyoc → San Blas artisan quarter. Fiestas Patrias week means parades and dancing in the plaza — join in.

twins.title: ChocoMuseo chocolate workshop
twins.description: Bean-to-bar workshop — the kids make their own chocolate, parents taste the single-origin dark. A low-effort high-fun afternoon at 3,400 m.

twins.title: Cusco city + 🎉 Fiestas Patrias
twins.notes: Jul 28 = Peruvian Independence Day — parades and celebrations on Plaza de Armas (festive bonus!). Expect celebratory crowds.

twins.title: Palcoyo full-day trip (5am–4pm)
twins.description:
3 colourful mountains, gentle 2 km walk at ~4,900 m — fine after 5+ days of altitude. Far fewer crowds than Vinicunca; llama/alpaca scenery.

The quieter rainbow mountain: a rolling **1.5–2 h loop** across three striped ridges — red, ochre, turquoise and violet strata — with the glacier-capped peak of Ausangate (6,384 m) as the backdrop. Palcoyo sits **~3 h from Cusco** (better road than Vinicunca), so it's a full-day outing: 5am pick-up, lunch back in the valley, early evening in Cusco. 4,800 m means slow steps, coca tea, and no rush — the kids manage it fine, and the llama herd that patrols the ridge is the family photo of the trip.

twins.title: Decide on the day
twins.description: Legs good? **Humantay Lake** (4,200 m, turquoise glacial lake, horse option at trailhead). Need a rest? **Cusco cooking class + San Pedro Market** (ceviche + lucuma juice — teen-approved).

twins.title: Flex — Humantay Lake OR cooking class
Museo Larco
twins.description: Pre-Columbian gold, beautiful gardens.

twins.title: La Mar — one last ceviche
twins.description: Or Astrid y Gastón.

twins.title: Malecón bike ride Miraflores → Barranco
twins.description: The clifftop cycle path from Miraflores to Barranco — paragliders overhead, Pacific below, sunset stop at the Bridge of Sighs.

twins.title: Magic Water Circuit at night
twins.description: 13 illuminated fountains in the Parque de la Reserva, including the world's largest fountain complex. Cheesy, spectacular, and the kids will love it.

twins.title: Chile + Peru — Summer 2027
twins.subtitle: Santiago · Valle Nevado ski days · Sacred Valley · Machu Picchu · Cusco · Lima
twins.summary:
Family trip (Niko + **Henri** 17 + **Renée** 15) combining **3–4 ski days at Valle Nevado** (Chile) with the Peru spine: **Lima → Sacred Valley → Machu Picchu → Cusco**. July is the only month where both countries are simultaneously at their seasonal best — Chilean winter ski peak AND Peruvian dry-season hiking peak.

The linchpin: **LATAM flies Santiago → Cusco non-stop** (daily, ~2h30–3h30), so the two halves stitch together without backtracking through Lima. Bonus: 3–4 days above 3,000 m at Valle Nevado pre-acclimatises everyone for Cusco (3,400 m).

**Stage: planned** — dates set (Sat Jul 17 → Mon Aug 2), nothing booked yet. Booking windows: international flights by Jan 2027, Valle Nevado by Mar 2027, Machu Picchu permits Jan–Feb 2027.

practical.notes:
⚠️ **Fiestas Patrias (Jul 28–29)** falls inside this window — Peruvian Independence Day: festive parades in Cusco/Lima, but trains, flights and hotels around those dates fill up and prices peak. Book PeruRail + internal flights before Jan 2027.

**Gear**: rent everything at Valle Nevado/Farellones (~$30–50/day pp) — Henri rents skis on-site too, so NO ski bags on the plane at all. Niko rents or brings only his board; nothing for Henri goes in the hold. **Altitude**: VN base 3,000 m / summit 3,670 m pre-acclimatises for Cusco (3,400 m); Sacred Valley (2,800 m) first, Cusco after. Budget delta over the Peru-only trip: ~+€4.5–7k → ~€15–19k family.
